display.title: Episode 267: The Storyteller, the Baal Shem Tov and the Feared Official (Adar)
display.summary_short: Adding joy in Adar, a first-grade class leads the Shema, Rabbi Yehudah begins his one remembered story about the Baal Shem Tov and a feared official, and what to pray for at candle lighting.
display.summary_long: Broadcast at the start of Adar 5747. Uncle Yossi explains 'mishenichnas Adar marbin b'simchah': we are always happy, but in Adar we add to our joy and make others happy too, especially by helping them do a mitzvah. He shares the Baal Shem Tov's lesson of the mirror: show a happy face and your friend, and Hashem Himself, will shine back at you. After the Hakochainik march, story time continues: Rabbi Yehudah, who has forgotten every story but one, sits by candlelight with the wealthy Reb Yitzchak and begins. He tells how the Baal Shem Tov took him to a city ruled by Alex, a feared official who issued harsh decrees and refused to see any Jew, and sent him to Alex's door to demand a meeting; he knocks, and the story pauses. A first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school leads the Shema and each girl says her name. In the mailbox, a girl who wants to join Tzivos Hashem writes out the Shema by heart. Mitzvah time teaches that after lighting Shabbos candles we look at the flames and ask Hashem for whatever we or our family need. The show ends with a furniture sponsor, candle time and the new Moshiach Times magazine.
display.lesson: In Adar we add to our joy and spread it to others; a happy face is reflected back by friends and by Hashem.
